text:
maria: quick heads up — after landing the kernel-selection change in runtime/commit 2f9a we see ~12-18% throughput drop on multi-gpu small-batch chat workloads (seq=32, batch=4). p50 up ~8ms, p95 up ~24ms.

sam: ugh. which GPUs and NCCL config?

maria: gpus: 8xA100-40GB, tensor parallel 2, pipeline parallel 1. Using channels=4 (runtime default), LL128 enabled. NCCL envs: NCCL_PROTO=LL128, NCCL_ALGO=ring, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1048576.

ravi: can you paste profiler snippet? nvprof / tracy output?

maria: pasted below (nvprof condensed):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel
0.45      ncclSend/Recv (small)
1.35      ncclAllReduce (sync)  <-- lots of small allreduce calls
2.10      cudaMemcpyAsync
0.12      attention_fwd_kernel
```
Also runtime trace: we increased kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused attention kernels which increase compute but apparently increase message fragmentation for KV cache updates.

sam: fragmentation for KV updates -> smaller tensors being allreduced more often. that increases allreduce overhead and reduces ability to overlap comm/compute.

jen: did we regress the batching heuristic? small requests used to coalesce better at the transport layer.

maria: yes, commit touched kernel batching boundaries to prefer lower latency per-kernel. seems to reduce aggregation opportunities.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert 1761234567: throughput -15% vs baseline 1759000000 on benchmark "chat-small-batch".

ravi: quick experiments to run: 1) flip NCCL_PROTO=LL (not LL128) 2) increase NCCL_BUFFSIZE 3) reduce channels to 2 4) force algorithm to tree (NCCL_ALGO=tree) and run nccl-tests/all_reduce_perf to measure small message perf.

sam: also try bumping NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD so small messages still use SIMPLE protocol (less handshake) — sometimes LL/LL128 overhead dominates for <8KB.

maria: running tests now. first run: channels=4, NCCL_PROTO=LL128 -> all_reduce (1KB msgs) avg latency 850us, overlap poor.

maria: channels=2, NCCL_PROTO=LL -> latency 620us, throughput +11% vs current.

maria: NCCL_ALGO=tree gave small improvement on 1KB messages but worse at 32KB (we have mix).

jen: sounds like our kernel-selection change created a higher variance in message sizes (many tiny updates). For mixed-size workloads a hybrid: SIMPLE for tiny, LL for mid, LL128 for large might help. Can we expose NCCL thresholds via runtime config and autotune?

ravi: yes. propose a quick runtime patch: 1) revert the batching boundary change for KV flush path 2) add NCCL_PROTO recommendation table in runtime config based on observed message size histogram 3) collect nccl-prof metrics in prod to validate.

maria: I put a draft PR: runtime: adaptive-nccl-proto by histogram (WIP). It toggles NCCL_PROTO per-model based on 99p message size.

sam: make sure we don’t spam env toggles per-request. do it per-VM or per-pool.

jen: also adding a micro-batcher that coalesces KV cache updates across concurrent requests into one allreduce when latency budget allows — should reduce small-allreduce frequency.

maria: ran micro-batcher prototype: for batch window 2ms, we saw 9% throughput gain and p95 down 18%.

ravi: nice. next steps: land micro-batcher + revert kernel boundary change for KV path, add NCCL proto heuristic, run full regression suite.

perf-bot: checklist created: #176123-adaptive-nccl -> run A/B on canary pool (50 pods) for 24h.

sam: can someone grab network counters during canary? I want to see if ring traffic increases and if we hit PCIe or NVLink saturation.

maria: on it. posting nccl topo + nvlink counters in a bit.

jen: thanks team. keeping this thread as the action log. reactions: :thumbsup:
